result:
REST, unless you already know your consumers need to compose deeply nested, highly variable queries.

HTTP caching, rate limiting and CDN behaviour work out of the box per URL and verb, whereas GraphQL sends everything through one POST endpoint and makes you build query-cost analysis, depth limits and persisted queries to protect yourself from expensive requests by strangers.

Every third-party developer can call REST with curl and an OpenAPI spec, which also generates SDKs and docs for you, while GraphQL asks them to learn a query language and adopt a client library.

GraphQL's real advantage, letting clients fetch exactly the fields they want across many related resources in one round trip, mostly pays off for your own front ends with varied screens, and you can add it later as a layer over the REST API if that need appears.
